What are Tian's total earnings if she works 9 hours per day for 5 days?

parts.latex:
A real estate agent's commission for selling houses is $2\%$ for the first \$800 000 of the sale price and $1.5\%$ for any amount over \$800 000.

Calculate the commission earned in selling a house for \$1 500 000.

solutions.latex:
The commission is $2\%$ of the first $\$800\,000$ plus $1.5\%$ of the amount over $\$800\,000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Commission} &= 0.02 \times 800\,000 + 0.015 \times (1\,500\,000 - 800\,000) \\ &= 0.02 \times 800\,000 + 0.015 \times 700\,000 \\ &= \$26\,500 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates a correct percentage, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Zazu works a 38-hour week and is paid at an hourly rate of \$45. Any overtime hours worked are paid at time-and-a-half.

In a particular week, Zazu worked the regular 38 hours and some overtime hours. In that week Zazu earned \$2790.

How many hours of overtime did Zazu work in that week?

solutions.latex:
Normal time earnings:
$$38\times 45=\$1710$$
Overtime paid:
$$2790-1710=\$1080$$
Overtime rate is time-and-a-half, $45\times 1.5$ per hour.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Overtime hours} &= \dfrac{1080}{45\times 1.5} \\ &= 16 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Zazu worked } 16 \text{ hours of overtime}$$
criteria: Finds Zazu's normal time earnings and overtime hourly rate, or equivalent merit

How much will she earn for a 4-hour shift with this increase?

solutions.latex:
A $2\%$ increase means the new rate is $102\%$ of the old rate.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{New rate} &= 28\times 1.02 \\ &= \$28.56 \text{ per hour} \end{aligned}$$
For a 4-hour shift:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Earnings} &= 4\times 28.56 \\ &= \$114.24 \end{aligned}$$
The answer is option D.

parts.latex:
Frankie takes four weeks of annual leave. His weekly pay is \$350 and his annual leave loading is $17\dfrac{1}{2}\%$ of four weeks pay.

What is Frankie's total pay for this period of annual leave?

solutions.latex:
Four weeks of pay:
$$4 \times \$350 = \$1400$$
The leave loading is $17\dfrac{1}{2}\%$ of this:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Loading} &= 0.175 \times \$1400 \\ &= \$245 \end{aligned}$$
Total pay for the period:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \$1400 + \$245 \\ &= \$1645.00 \end{aligned}$$
So the answer is option D.

Songwriters are paid a royalty for each of their songs that are included on an album.

For each individual song on an album, they are paid 6.25% of the albums retail price divided by the total number of songs on the album.

Emily wrote seven of the nine songs on her bands first album. The album retails for \$15.99 as a download, CD or vinyl.

How much will she earn in song writing royalties, if the album sold 12 450 copies over all formats?

solutions.latex:
Royalty for one song on one copy:
$$\dfrac{6.25\%\times 15.99}{9}$$
Emily wrote 7 songs and 12 450 copies were sold, so the total is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Royalty} &= 7\times 12\,450\times \dfrac{0.0625\times 15.99}{9} \\ &\approx \$9\,677.28 \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.

6473.stem: Louie is a real estate agent earning a retainer of \$600 per week.

parts.latex: Find Louie’s monthly retainer.

Every month Louie also earns a commission at a rate of $R\%$ on the first \$500 000 of his sales, and then at half of that rate on any sales above \$500 000.

Louie’s monthly income after selling \$750 000 worth of property is \$17 600.

Find the value of $R$.

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year and 12 months.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{monthly retainer}&=(600\times 52)\div 12\\&=\$2600\end{aligned}$$

Commission is $R\%$ on the first \$500 000 and $\dfrac{R}{2}\%$ on the remaining \$250 000. Add the retainer of \$2600 to equal \$17 600.
$$\begin{aligned}\left(\dfrac{R}{100}\times 500\,000\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{R}{100}\times 250\,000\right)+2600&=17\,600\\5000R+1250R&=15\,000\\6250R&=15\,000\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore R=2.4$$
criteria: Forms a valid equation to calculate the rate of commission

Linda is a sales representative and earns \$750 per week plus a commission based on her sales of any amount over \$2500 per week.

In a particular week, Linda's sales were \$3000 and she earned \$850 including her commission.

What percentage commission did Linda receive from her employer?

solutions.latex:
Commission is paid only on sales over $\$2500$.

Sales over $\$2500$:
$$\$3000-\$2500=\$500$$
Commission earned:
$$\$850-\$750=\$100$$
Commission rate:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{100}{500}\times 100\% &= 20\% \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the commission is } 20\% \text{ (option D)}$$

parts.latex:
Trai works as a waiter in a restaurant. He gets paid as follows:

Normal pay - \$18 per hour

Time & half pay - weekday hours after 6 pm

Double pay - all hours worked at the weekend

In a week that he works 30 hours at normal pay, 6 hours after 6 pm and $x$ hours at the weekend, Trai gets paid a total of \$1062. What is the value of $x$ ?

solutions.latex:
Normal pay:
$$30\times 18=\$540$$
Time and a half is $1.5\times 18=\$27$ per hour, so the 6 hours after 6 pm pay:
$$6\times 27=\$162$$
Double pay is $2\times 18=\$36$ per hour, so the weekend hours pay $36x$.

Total pay:
$$\begin{aligned} 540+162+36x &= 1062 \\ 36x &= 360 \\ x &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=10 \text{ (option A)}$$

7533.stem:
Jo delivered catalogues as a job during her summer holidays.

She was paid a rate of $\$20$ per 1000 catalogues.

On an average day she delivered 4 catalogues to each residence along 45 city blocks.

Each block had on average 40 residences to receive catalogues.

parts.latex: What would she have been paid for a week where she worked on 3 days?
It took her on average 12 minutes to cover each block. What hourly rate of pay would be equivalent to her piecework pay rate?

solutions.latex:
Number of catalogues over 3 days:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{No. of catalogues}&=3\times4\times45\times40 \\ &=21\,600 \end{aligned}$$
Pay at $\$20$ per 1000 catalogues:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Pay}&=21\,600\times\dfrac{20}{1000} \\ &=\$432 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the number of catalogues, or equivalent merit
